breakfast.name: Käsknöpfle (Cheese Spaetzle)
instructions: Make spaetzle batter
Press through spaetzle maker into boiling water
Layer cooked spaetzle with cheese
Top with caramelized onions and butter
Serve with applesauce

breakfast.name: Birchermüesli
instructions: Soak oats in milk overnight
Mix with yogurt, apple, honey
Top with nuts and berries

breakfast.name: Züpfe (Braided Butter Bread)
instructions: Make enriched yeast dough with butter, milk, eggs — very soft
Let rise 1-2 hours
Divide into two or three long ropes
Braid loosely — the braiding should be visible after baking
Brush generously with egg wash
Bake until deeply golden — the braid pattern should be pronounced
The crust should be glossy and golden-brown
The crumb inside is rich from butter and egg
Züpfe is the Sunday bread of German-speaking Switzerland and Liechtenstein
The braided shape is cultural and religious — Sunday blessing bread
The rich, buttery soft crumb is the reward for the braid technique
breakfast.description: Liechtenstein's Sunday braided bread — enriched butter-and-egg dough braided and baked until glossy golden. The braid is cultural: Sunday blessing bread across German-speaking Alpine regions. The rich, soft crumb from butter and egg is the reward. Sliced for Sunday breakfast with butter and honey.

breakfast.name: Rohrnudeln (Baked Yeast Dumplings)
ingredients: Vanilla sauce or plum compote for serving
instructions: Make a rich yeast dough — well-enriched with butter and eggs
Let rise 1 hour
Shape into smooth balls — they should be round and tight
Place in a well-buttered deep baking dish — touching each other
Let rise again 30 minutes — they expand and press together
The touching is important — they support each other as they rise and bake
Bake at 175°C until golden on top
The tops should be golden, the undersides steamed-soft from the pan
Serve with vanilla sauce or plum compote
Rohrnudeln are the Alpine sweet bun — found in Austria, Liechtenstein, Bavaria
The touching-buns-in-pan method and the steam-soft bottoms are the appeal
breakfast.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine baked buns — rich yeast dumplings placed touching in a deep buttered dish, rising until they press against each other, baking until golden on top and steam-soft beneath. The crowded pan gives a pull-apart texture. Served with vanilla sauce or plum compote, rohrnudeln are the Alpine sweet morning luxury.

lunch.name: Hafalaab (Cornmeal Semolina Soup)
instructions: Toast cornmeal and semolina in butter
Add water and milk
Simmer until thick porridge
Season with salt

lunch.name: Ribel (Corn Porridge)
instructions: Cook cornmeal in milk and water
Stir until thick
Fry in butter until crispy bits form
Serve sweet with fruit or savory with cheese
lunch.description: Crispy-edged corn porridge — sweet or savory.

lunch.name: Sauerkrautsuppe (Sauerkraut Soup)
instructions: Dice smoked pork, saute with onion
Add sauerkraut, potatoes, caraway seeds, bay
Cover with water or pork stock
Simmer 25 minutes until potatoes are soft
The sauerkraut provides acidity; the smoked pork provides depth
The caraway seed is the Alpine accent — it connects this soup to the region
Finish with a swirl of sour cream
Sauerkrautsuppe is Alpine winter warming — Liechtenstein's version of a regional classic
The sauerkraut acidity brightened by sour cream is deeply warming
A small country's small winter soup, but reliable and complete
lunch.description: Liechtenstein's winter sauerkraut soup — smoked pork simmered with fermented cabbage, potatoes, and caraway seeds into a warming, slightly tart broth. The caraway seed is the Alpine accent. Sauerkrautsuppe is a shared regional dish from Liechtenstein through Austria and Bavaria, each version barely different from the next.

lunch.name: Knöpfle (Alpine Cheese Spaetzle)
instructions: Make batter: flour, eggs, water, salt — looser than pasta dough
Press through a spaetzle press or colander holes into boiling salted water
The little noodles cook in 2-3 minutes, float when done
Drain, toss in butter
Layer in a baking dish: spaetzle, grated cheese, spaetzle, cheese
Bake briefly until cheese melts
Top with caramelized onions and chives
Knöpfle is Liechtenstein's version of Käsknöpfle (already in breakfast) — same dish, different serving
The spaetzle-cheese-onion combination is Alpine comfort food's peak expression
Liechtenstein's national dish is technically Käsknöpfle — it appears in multiple forms
lunch.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine cheese spaetzle — tiny soft noodles layered with melting Gruyère and topped with caramelized onions. Effectively the same dish as Käsknöpfle but served as a main course rather than breakfast. The spaetzle-cheese-caramelized onion combination is Alpine comfort food's highest expression.

lunch.name: Fürstenlaibli (Prince's Roll)
instructions: Mix wheat and rye flour — the rye gives a slightly dense, chewy crumb
Make a yeast dough — well-fermented for flavor
Shape into small oval rolls
Score the top with a single slash
Brush with water or milk
Top with caraway or sesame
Bake in a hot oven until the crust cracks along the score
The mixed flour crumb should have texture — not purely white bread soft
Fürstenlaibli (Prince's roll) is a Liechtenstein-specific bread roll
The prince reference connects this bread to Liechtenstein's princely family
lunch.description: Liechtenstein's prince's bread roll — mixed wheat-rye dough shaped into small ovals, scored and topped with caraway seeds. The rye flour gives a slightly chewy, dense crumb with more character than white rolls. The princely name connects this roll to Liechtenstein's ruling family and their small country's pride.

dinner.name: Fleischkäse (Meat Loaf)
instructions: Mix meats with all ingredients
Press into loaf pan
Bake at 175°C 60 min
Slice thick
Serve with potato salad

dinner.name: Raclette
instructions: Melt raclette cheese under heat
Scrape onto boiled potatoes
Serve with pickles and onions

dinner.name: Ribelmais (Cornmeal Dish)
ingredients: Optional: apple sauce, sugar for sweet version
instructions: Bring milk or water to a boil with salt and butter
Add cornmeal gradually — stir to prevent lumps
Cook 15-20 minutes until very thick
Serve as a thick porridge or let cool and slice like polenta
The cornmeal is Liechtenstein and eastern Switzerland's traditional grain
Not the Italian polenta — the local cornmeal is coarser
Sweet version: served with apple sauce or sugar and butter
Ribelmais is Liechtenstein's most ancient grain — pre-potato staple food
Corn cultivation arrived in Europe from the Americas via the Alpine trade routes
Liechtenstein's cornmeal culture is documented from the 17th century
dinner.description: Liechtenstein's ancestral cornmeal — coarse-ground corn cooked into a thick porridge or set and sliced. The local cornmeal culture predates the potato as the Alpine starch. Served savory with butter or sweet with apple sauce. Eastern Switzerland and Liechtenstein share this maize heritage, distinct from Italian polenta in texture and context.

dinner.name: Wurst und Sauerkraut (Sausage and Sauerkraut)
instructions: Caramelize onion in lard or butter
Add sauerkraut, white wine, juniper berries, caraway seeds
Simmer 15 minutes — the sauerkraut softens and the wine brightens it
Add sausages on top — cover and steam them in the sauerkraut vapors
The sausages heat through and absorb some of the sauerkraut fragrance
Serve together directly from the pan
Wurst und sauerkraut is German-Austrian-Swiss-Liechtenstein communal cooking
The juniper berry and caraway accent is the Alpine refinement
Simple, reliable, deeply satisfying in cold Alpine weather
The sauerkraut acidity cuts through the sausage fat perfectly
dinner.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine sausage plate — sausages steamed over sauerkraut seasoned with juniper berries and caraway in white wine. The juniper-caraway Alpine accent lifts the simple combination. A shared dish of the German-speaking Alpine world, reliable in every cold-weather month.

dinner.name: Polenta mit Käse (Cornmeal with Cheese)
instructions: Cook cornmeal in milk and water — creamy version
Stir in generous butter
Add grated Gruyère — stir until melted and incorporated
The cheese-cornmeal combination is thick, rich, and deeply savory
Season well
Serve immediately — cornmeal sets as it cools
Top with crispy bacon if desired
Polenta mit käse is Liechtenstein's cheese-enriched cornmeal
The Gruyère or Appenzeller gives an intense, Alpine-style cheese depth
The combination of Alpine cheese and cornmeal is uniquely this small Alpine region
dinner.description: Liechtenstein's cheese-enriched cornmeal — creamy cornmeal stirred with Alpine Gruyère or Appenzeller cheese until thick and deeply savory. The Alpine cheese culture (Gruyère, Appenzeller, Emmental) meeting the cornmeal tradition creates the most characteristically Liechtenstein dish: two Alpine staples combined.

snacks.name: Kartoffelpuffer (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Squeeze moisture from potatoes
Mix with egg, flour, onion
Fry flattened patties until crispy

snacks.name: Krapfen (Alpine Fried Doughnut)
instructions: Make enriched yeast dough
Rise 1 hour
Roll out and cut into circles
Place jam in center of half the circles
Top with another circle, seal edges firmly
Let rise 30 minutes
Deep fry at 170°C until golden on both sides
Roll in powdered sugar immediately
The jam should be sealed inside — a burst of jam mid-doughnut
Krapfen are the Alpine Fasching (carnival) doughnut
Made before Lent as a fat-consuming celebration treat
Every Alpine country (Austria, Bavaria, Liechtenstein) makes them at Fasching
snacks.description: Liechtenstein's carnival doughnut — yeast-risen dough filled with apricot jam, deep-fried until golden, and rolled in powdered sugar. Made for Fasching (carnival) before Lent as a fat-consuming celebration. The hidden jam center that bursts in your mouth and the powdered sugar cloud are the Alpine doughnut hallmarks.

snacks.name: Alpkäse (Alpine Cheese)
instructions: Slice Alpine cheese thickly — it should be semi-firm
Serve with dark rye bread and butter
Pickled accompaniments cut through the richness
Alpkäse is made from summer pasture milk — cows grazing at altitude
Summer pasture milk has more flavor from wild Alpine herbs
The cheese reflects the herbs the cows ate — thyme, gentian, wild garlic
Liechtenstein's Alpine summer dairy is a recognized tradition
Eating alpkäse with rye bread is the mountain farmer's afternoon snack
The cheese's complexity from summer pasture herbs is the whole story
No cooking required — just good cheese, good bread, good context
snacks.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine cheese plate — summer pasture cheese (from cows grazing high Alpine meadows) served with rye bread and pickled vegetables. The Alpine summer pasture gives the milk — and thus the cheese — flavor from wild herbs the cows consume: thyme, gentian, wild garlic. No recipe needed, just exceptional ingredients.

snacks.name: Schöfeli (Fried Bread Rolls)
instructions: Slice stale bread rolls
Dip in egg-milk mixture
Fry in butter until golden — French toast style
Sprinkle cinnamon-sugar
Serve with jam or apple sauce
Schöfeli are Liechtenstein's French toast equivalent
The stale bread transformation is Alpine thrift culture — waste nothing
The cinnamon-sugar crust with apple sauce is distinctly Alpine
A simple Alpine after-school snack elevated by good butter
Every Alpine household had a version — the names differ but the principle is the same
snacks.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine French toast — stale bread rolls dipped in egg and milk, fried in butter, and dusted with cinnamon sugar. Alpine thrift culture at work: stale bread transformed into something better. The cinnamon-apple sauce pairing is the distinctly Alpine finishing touch.

desserts.name: Pastete (Puff Pastry Tart)
instructions: Line tart mold with pastry
Fill with custard
Bake at 180°C 30 min
Top with preserves
desserts.description: Puff pastry tart with custard and fruit.

desserts.name: Apfelkuchen (Apple Cake)
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs
Add flour and baking powder — a smooth batter
Peel and slice apples — arrange into the batter or fold in
Dust with cinnamon and lemon zest
Bake at 175°C until a toothpick comes out clean
The apples should be soft and fragrant
Dust with powdered sugar when cooled
Apfelkuchen is the Alpine cake par excellence — apple orchards everywhere
Every Alpine grandmother has her specific version
The Liechtenstein version is simple, not layered — the apple quality is the difference
The apple harvest is a significant moment in Alpine rural calendars
desserts.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine apple cake — simple butter cake with tart apple slices baked through until soft and fragrant with cinnamon. The Alpine apple harvest culture makes this the region's most important cake. The quality of the apple (tart, local varieties) is the difference between a good and great Apfelkuchen.

desserts.name: Fasnachtsküchlein (Carnival Pastry)
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, cream, sugar, salt, optional brandy into a stiff dough
Rest 30 minutes
Roll very thin — as thin as possible
Cut into shapes: strips with holes, bow-ties, stars
Fry at 175°C until golden and slightly puffed
Drain and dust immediately with powdered sugar
Fasnachtsküchlein are Liechtenstein's Fasching (carnival) pastries
Made in huge quantities before Lent — to be consumed freely
The crispy, airy fried pastry with powdered sugar is addictive
A German-speaking Alpine tradition — Liechtenstein, Switzerland, Austria, Bavaria all share it
desserts.description: Liechtenstein's Fasching pastry — thin dough fried until crispy and airy, dusted in powdered sugar. Made in large quantities before Lent as part of the carnival consumption tradition. The thin, crispy, powdered-sugar fried pastry is a shared German-speaking Alpine tradition. The brandy in the dough creates extra crispiness.

desserts.name: Rahmkuchen (Cream Tart)
instructions: Line a tart tin with shortcrust pastry
Make cream filling: mix thick cream, eggs, sugar, vanilla
Pour cream filling into the pastry shell
Dust with cinnamon
Bake at 175°C until the cream sets and the top has a golden skin
The cream should be barely set — it jiggles slightly in center
Cool completely before cutting — it firms as it cools
Rahmkuchen is the Alpine cream tart — similar to a Tarte Tatin but cream-focused
The richness of Alpine dairy makes this extraordinary — the cream quality matters
Simple but indulgent — the cream is the ingredient
desserts.description: Liechtenstein's cream tart — thick Alpine cream custard in a shortcrust shell, dusted with cinnamon, baked until just set. The quality of Alpine dairy (grass-fed, summer pasture cows) makes the cream uniquely rich. A simple tart that asks only for exceptional cream.

drinks.name: Heida Wine
instructions: Serve chilled in wine glass
Pair with Käsknöpfle or Raclette
drinks.description: Crisp Alpine white wine from Liechtenstein's small vineyards.

drinks.name: Glühwein (Mulled Wine)
instructions: Heat wine with spices and orange
Do not boil
Sweeten, strain
Serve warm
drinks.description: Warm spiced wine — an Alpine winter essential.

drinks.name: Heida Spätlese (Late Harvest Wine)
ingredients: Heida (Savagnin blanc) grapes grown in Liechtenstein and Valais
Late harvest (Spätlese) — picked after first frost
instructions: Heida is one of Europe's rarest grape varieties — grows only in high Alpine sites
Late harvest: grapes left on the vine past normal harvest
The frost concentrates the sugars — sweeter, more complex wine
Pour into a wine glass, serve at 10-12°C
The wine is golden, honey-scented, with mineral Alpine freshness
Best sipped slowly, paired with Alpine cheeses or Apfelkuchen
Liechtenstein has a tiny but proud wine tradition — 11 hectares of vines
Heida is the variety that thrives at Liechtenstein's altitude
Late harvest Heida is a collector's wine — limited, precious
The concentrated honey-mineral flavor is the Alpine late-harvest signature
drinks.description: Liechtenstein's rarest wine — Heida (Savagnin blanc) grown at high Alpine altitude, late-harvested after frost concentrates the sugars into a golden, honey-mineral wine. Liechtenstein has only 11 hectares of vineyards. The Heida grape is one of Europe's rarest and the late-harvest style maximizes its alpine character.

drinks.name: Alpenkräutertee (Alpine Herb Tea)
ingredients: Dried Alpine herbs: linden flower, chamomile, thyme, yarrow
instructions: Blend dried Alpine herbs — each has a specific character
Linden flower: floral, calming
Chamomile: classic, soothing
Thyme: warming, slightly medicinal
Steep in boiling water 5-8 minutes
Add honey while still warm
The tea should be herbal but not medicinal-tasting
Serve with a piece of Apfelkuchen or cheese
Alpine herb teas are Liechtenstein and Swiss Alpine tradition
The herb knowledge (which plants, when to harvest) is cultural inheritance
The specific combination of Alpine herbs is each family's tradition
drinks.description: Liechtenstein's Alpine herbal tea — a blend of linden flower, chamomile, thyme, and yarrow steeped until fragrant, sweetened with honey. The specific blend is each Alpine family's cultural inheritance. The knowledge of which herbs to pick and when to harvest is Alpine traditional knowledge passed through generations.
